## [0.26.0] - 2026-10-29

### Added

- **Project Map: compact folder chains, Reveal Active File, and keyboard reach (Map review).**
  - A chain of single-child folders (`src/main/java/com/acme`) opens with one click and shows as one column titled
    `src / main / java / com / acme`; each folder stays in the breadcrumb, and Left/Backspace step back through it.
    ⋯ → **Compact folder chains** turns it off.
  - New command **Project Map: Reveal Active File** (`projectMap.revealActiveFile`) opens or raises the Map window on
    the file being edited, and ⋯ → **Always select opened file** (off) follows every file you open. A Map opened with
    nothing selected starts at the current file.
  - ⋯ → **Single-click opens files** (on): turn it off to select a file with a click and open it with a double-click
    or Enter.
  - **Shift+Enter** opens or closes the selected file's or declaration's preview card, and the row menu (right-click,
    Menu key, Shift+F10) gains **Preview**, **Show/Hide Structure**, **Personal Notes** and **Close Column**.
  - Cards, note cards and sticky notes move with **Alt+arrows**, and cards and note cards resize with
    **Alt+Shift+arrows**; a card's menu has **Move to Free Space**.
  - The ⋯ options are remembered per workspace, as is a maximized Map window (workspace schema 26 → 27).
  - The **?** popover lists every gesture and key, including cards, notes and filters, with key names in your
    language.
- **HTML: links, markup checks and colour swatches** (HTML review: links).
  - Go to Definition and Ctrl-click on an `href` or `src` open the file it names, at the element whose `id` its
    `#fragment` names; a `#fragment` alone moves in the page, a web address goes to the browser after asking, and a
    missing file says "File not found: missing.html" instead of "No definition found". Works with the HTML language
    server (its document links) and without one or with LSP off (the value resolved against the page).
  - Editora checks an HTML page's markup itself: an element that is never closed, an end tag that closes nothing,
    and a local link whose file does not exist are marked as warnings (source "editora"). With the HTML server they
    join its diagnostics in the Problems window; without it they show as squiggles in the page. Void elements,
    optional end tags (`<li>`, `<p>`, `<td>` …), `<script>`/`<style>` content, comments and web addresses never
    count. Settings → Editor → "HTML markup checks" (on) turns it off.
  - Related File from a page offers the stylesheets and scripts it loads (`<link href>`, `<script src>`) first, and
    from a stylesheet or script the project's pages that load it.
  - A CSS colour in a stylesheet, a `<style>` block or a `style=""` gets a small swatch in its colour before it, from
    the HTML and CSS servers' colour provider.
- **Java: library sources.** A Maven library's sources are fetched as its class opens, when a repository has them.
  A library class that has none, shown decompiled (a `lib/` or system jar, an artifact only installed locally, a JDK
  without `src.zip`), says so in its tab, with **Download Sources** for one a repository may have and **Choose
  Sources…** to attach a `-sources.jar` or zip from disk (also LSP: Download Library Sources and LSP: Choose Library
  Sources… in the palette); a Gradle library is told its sources come from its build. A tab whose library gets its
  sources later shows them at once, every open tab of that library or JDK. Settings → LSP has "Download library
  sources when a Java project is imported" (off; Maven), applied at the next import, and View: Toggle Downloading
  Library Sources at Import flips it. Looking for a Maven library's sources can ask Maven Central's search, by the
  jar's checksum. Settings schema 153 → 154.
- **Project Map: Personal Notes on preview cards.** Selecting text in a Map preview (a file's or a declaration's)
  brings up a floating bar, as in a Markdown buffer, whose **Add Personal Note** button notes the selection. A Notes
  button before **Open** in the card's title bar counts the notes on what the card shows and sticks them beside it as
  sticky notes, one editable sheet per note, each tied by a connector to its line, which is marked in the same amber an
  editor tab marks a note's text with; they move, resize and zoom with the
  card, can be dragged to another spot beside it, save as a note card does, follow "Hide all open Personal Notes", and
  close with it. A note added from a card brings its notes up. The Personal Notes card no longer lets the map show
  through it on themes whose amber tint is translucent.
- **Project Map: Hide unmatched.** A checkbox in the Map's filter row takes the rows the filters would fade off the
  map, leaving only the matches and the folders that lead to them. It never hides silently: an amber "N rows hidden"
  badge sits beside it, and each column shows "shown/total" with an "N hidden" line under its rows. An open preview or
  note card goes with its row and comes back with it. Remembered per workspace (workspace schema 24 → 25).
- **Terminal: Nerd Font icons without installing a Nerd Font.** Editora bundles Symbols Nerd Font Mono (Nerd Fonts
  3.5.1), so the icons eza, lsd and powerline prompts print show on any machine. An installed Nerd Font build of the
  terminal's font still wins. Bundled icons are drawn a cell and a half wide, the size Nerd Font builds give them;
  Powerline separators stay at text size. Licences in NOTICE.
- **Terminal: the kitty keyboard protocol.** A program that asks for it (Neovim, Helix, fish, nushell) gets
  unambiguous keys: Escape on its own, Ctrl+I apart from Tab, Shift+Enter as a key, and with its further flags
  repeats, releases and the text each key types. Everything else keeps the legacy bytes.
- **Terminal selection:** dragging past the top or bottom edge scrolls faster the further out the pointer is;
  **Alt+drag** (Option on macOS, Ctrl+Alt where the window manager takes Alt) selects a block of columns, copied one
  row per line; **Copy on select** (Settings ▸ Terminal, off); on Linux a selection sets the PRIMARY selection and a
  middle-click pastes it (wl-copy/wl-paste, xclip or xsel), elsewhere middle-click pastes the clipboard;
  **Shift+Insert** pastes and **Ctrl+Insert** copies.
- **Terminal: desktop notifications from programs** (OSC 9, OSC 777): a build saying it has finished marks its tab
  and, unless you are looking at that terminal, reaches the desktop (notify-send or the session bus, osascript, a
  PowerShell toast). One per terminal every two seconds; Settings ▸ Terminal ▸ Desktop notifications turns the
  desktop half off.
- **Terminal: programs can copy to the clipboard** (OSC 52), as tmux and editors do over SSH. A program can never
  read the clipboard. Settings ▸ Terminal ▸ Let programs copy to the clipboard (on). Settings schema 149 → 150
  (additive).
- **Terminal tabs name the program running in them** (vim, npm, ssh) when the shell set no title, before the
  folder's name.
- **Terminal theme** (Settings ▸ Terminal ▸ Theme, `terminalTheme`): the integrated terminal's colours, chosen
  apart from the editor theme. **Editor theme**, the default, keeps today's palette derived from the editor's
  syntax colours; Solarized Dark/Light, Dracula, Nord, Gruvbox Dark/Light, One Half Dark/Light, Tango Dark/Light,
  Campbell and the Editora pair are fixed schemes that stay the same whichever editor theme is active. Open
  terminals recolour at once. Settings schema 147 → 148 (additive).
- **XML: Generate Grammar….** Generates an XSD, DTD or RELAX NG grammar from the current XML file and binds the
  file to it, with "Files without a grammar" left at Nothing (lemminx offered these fixes only on its no-grammar
  hint). In Structure, a DTD now lists its elements with their attributes, its entities and notations.
- **Bash server settings (Bash review, config).** Settings ▸ LSP ▸ Bash has **Lint with ShellCheck** and
  **Format with shfmt** switches (on; off sends the server an empty path and silences the missing-tool notices) and
  **Explain source lines the server cannot follow** (on: a hint on `source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"` lines saying to
  add a `# shellcheck source=` directive). A project's `bashIde` object now also passes `enableSourceErrorDiagnostics`,
  `globPattern`, `logLevel`, `shellcheckExternalSources`, `backgroundAnalysisIgnore` and `shfmt.additionalArguments`
  (checked for type; unknown keys only in a trusted folder), and `"shellcheckPath": ""` / `"shfmt": {"path": ""}`
  turn a tool off. Background analysis also reads `.ksh`, `.mksh` and `.bats` files. Settings schema 152 → 153.

### Changed

- **Project Map: the first column is the project's own files (Map review).** The one-row "Project" column is gone:
  the first column lists the project's files and folders under the project's name. Click that title (or the first
  breadcrumb) to select the project folder and right-click it for the folder's menu; Home selects the first row.
- **Project Map: names and text.** Long names are cut in the middle (a row is at most 360 px wide; the tooltip has
  the full name), rows faded by a filter keep readable labels, the canvas uses the UI font, toolbar text follows
  the UI size, and the back, forward and help buttons are larger targets. Map cards use the editor font and keep
  the last text zoom. Git "untracked" and "renamed" colours and the Structure tint read well on dark themes.
- **Project tree and Map: numbered files sort by number** (note-2 before note-10).
- **Project Map: Type buckets.** Plain-text documents (README, LICENSE, `.txt`) count as Markup, and build files
  (`go.mod`, `Gemfile`, Gradle and Maven wrappers, `*.gradle`, `.plist`) as Config.
- **Project and Map search finds the file you name first** (`Settings.java` for "Settings"), searches the whole
  project instead of stopping at the first 300 hits, and says when it shows only the best matches. A one-letter
  Map search filters the rows on the map instead of opening hundreds of folders.
- **Project Map: Clear** also clears the search and no longer turns off "Hide all open Personal Notes"; in German
  and Italian it reads "Zurücksetzen" / "Azzera".
- **Project Map: the Modified chip is now Unsaved.** It always matched files with unsaved changes; next to the Git "M"
  letter it read as Git-modified, which is what Git changed matches.
- **Project Map: every workspace starts left to right.** A workspace that stored right to left, the default saved by
  builds before 0.20.0, now opens left to right; picking right to left again is remembered.
  Workspace schema 25 → 26.
- **Terminal: a keystroke no longer clears the selection.** It goes when the text under it is redrawn, so a
  selection of the output above the prompt survives typing a command.
- **Terminal: a selection highlights exactly what it copies.** The highlight was a cell wider than the copied text,
  and a drag now ends at the cell boundary nearest the pointer.
- **Project Map: Structure columns have their own colour.** A file's Structure column, and the columns of
  declarations opened from it, sit on a faint violet card with violet-tinted rows, so they no longer look like
  folder columns (the overview tints them too). Themes can retune it with `.project-map-probe-structure`.
- **Simple mode: the toggle sits beside Settings.** The Simple-mode toolbar button moved to the right end of the
  toolbar, just left of Settings, and is no longer part of the customizable icon group, so a narrow window cannot
  push it into the overflow menu. A saved toolbar layout that lists it drops it on load.

### Fixed

- **Project Map window (Map review).**
  - In the No Project window the Map keeps the folder it was opened on: opening a file from it, or switching to a
    tab in another folder or an untitled tab, no longer re-roots it (losing its columns and cards) or closes it.
  - A Map window closed with its project reopens with the project in the same session, and one left open reopens
    at startup even with the Project tool window closed.
  - A card that mirrors an open file keeps following its edits after the Map window is closed and reopened, and a
    closed Map no longer polls cards, re-reads buffers or repaints on every tab switch.
  - An editor-theme switch reaches an open Map window and floating tool windows.
  - Print and PDF dialogs open over the Map window; a map just over one page is shrunk slightly (labels down to
    6 pt) instead of split, and the status says how many pages it took.
  - New Folder and New File from a Map row show and select the result; renaming to a taken name says so, and a
    case-only rename works on case-insensitive disks; a folder the Map cannot read is reported in the status bar;
    the Map commands say when Project support is off.
- **Project Map loading and search (Map review).**
  - An outside change made just after a rename, move, delete or new folder in Editora shows in the tree and the
    Map instead of being lost.
  - Opening a folder no longer re-reads every open folder (listings are cached per watched folder), and a folder
    that stops responding shows "Not responding" instead of freezing the Map's loading.
  - A folder the 1,200-row limit cannot fit stays open with a "Not loaded" row and fills in once a column closes.
  - Renaming or moving a folder while the Map is loading keeps it open, and preview and note cards follow a file
    renamed in Editora.
  - A column filter in a long folder searches the whole folder, the Git chip matches files inside a new untracked
    folder (with their "U"), and the search matches declarations in open Structure columns.
- **Project Map navigation (Map review).**
  - A search's first match, a breadcrumb, Back/Forward and a reveal scroll the selected row into view, even when its
    folder had to load first. Escape on the search returns to the row selected before it.
  - With Hide unmatched, the selection moves to the nearest row still shown; after "+N more…" it continues at the
    first new row.
  - The overview fits the map's shape, can be dragged, never pans into empty space, stays above cards, and is
    hidden in small windows; cards never cover the zoom bar.
  - A column blocked by its neighbour moves at once when dragged back, and a drag that starts on a row pans.
  - Tab skips off-screen column controls, and closing or tabbing out of a card returns the keyboard to the map.
  - Screen readers hear the selected row's states and its place among the visible rows instead of an empty tree.
  - Drawing happens at most once per frame and reuses the layout when only the view moves, so hovering, arrow keys
    and reloads stay smooth on large maps.
- **Project Map cards and notes (Map review).**
  - Note and bookmark shortcuts typed in a card (`C-c n`, `C-c m` in Emacs) mark the card's file instead of the
    active tab's; Add Personal Note on a card asks over the Map window and names the file and lines; the Menu-key
    menu of a card acts on the caret's line.
  - A card opens where it covers least, never over the columns leading to its row or where its next column opens.
  - A declaration card keeps its lines when its declaration is deleted, follows it when lines move above it, and
    follows an edited signature; methods are labelled with their parameter types, so inserting an overload no
    longer switches an open card to another method.
  - Structure columns list one-line members in every language, CSS selectors and at-rules, and YAML keys such as
    `on:`; a file past the read cap says its outline is partial; `.http` cards show the request's headers and body;
    `#` comments above a declaration belong to its card.
  - Card notes follow edits made outside Editora; many notes collapse into a "+K more notes" sheet and the Notes
    button counts them all; note cards head each note with its line, which opens the file there; the Notes button
    explains when "Hide all open Personal Notes" hides them.
  - Binary files and oversized images get a compact facts card; long files are coloured up to a line the status
    names; a card mirroring unsaved edits says so; Copy reads "Copy All" with nothing selected.
  - Cards share two loader threads and no longer re-read unchanged buffers every second.
  - Failures the Map recovers from but did not expect now reach the debug log.
- **HTML completion and popups (HTML review: comp).**
  - Enter and Tab accept an HTML tag, attribute or CSS property again while its documentation is showing. The docs'
    "MDN Reference" link took those keys (Enter opened the browser, Tab moved between links). Links in the
    completion docs, hovers, signature help and note hovers are now followed by a click only, for every language.
  - A hover opens at its first line instead of scrolled to the link at its end.
  - Completion docs from the HTML, CSS, Python and Java servers arrive as Markdown: links, code and the Baseline
    badge instead of a bare "MDN Reference: https://…" line.
  - Structure, Go to Symbol and breadcrumbs keep repeated sibling elements in an HTML page (every link of a nav, a
    second `<script>` and its functions).
  - In a page's `<style>` the snippets offered are CSS's, in a `<script>` JavaScript's, and inside a tag none: `col`
    no longer preselects `<col>` above `color`, nor `<a hr` the `<hr>` snippet.
  - Typing a closer by hand where Editora already inserted one (`<p>a</`) no longer opens a list whose Enter renamed
    `</p>` to `</body>`.
  - Accepting a CSS property opens the list of its values, and accepting a folder in a path the list of its files,
    as the server asks.
  - In an HTML start tag, typing `=` after an attribute name inserts `""` with the caret inside (with Auto-close
    tags on); a `"` typed straight after is taken as the opening quote.
- **HTML: Format Document keeps `<pre>`, `<code>` and `<textarea>` as written** (HTML review B2). The HTML server
  is now sent VS Code's defaults for its settings; before, it got none, and formatting collapsed the spaces in
  preformatted text and textarea values.
- **HTML: Format Document keeps the final newline and wraps at the file's `max_line_length`** (A3). The file's
  EditorConfig `insert_final_newline` decides, else the newline the file has; `max_line_length` (or `off`) sets the
  wrap column, else Settings → LSP → HTML (120).
- **HTML: completion no longer offers a closing tag Editora already inserted** (D3). The server is told Editora closes
  tags itself, and told again when the auto-close setting changes.
- **Settings → LSP → HTML** (A4): wrap column, attribute wrapping, elements whose content is kept as written,
  quotes for completed attributes, and checking embedded scripts and styles. A project can override them with an
  `html` object in `.editora/settings.json` (VS Code's key names). Settings schema 154 → 155.
- **HTML Live Preview (HTML review: preview).**
  - A video, archive or other big file next to the page no longer loads whole into Editora's memory (it could run
    out of memory): files are streamed, with byte ranges, so `<video>` and `<audio>` play and seek (Safari too),
    and media, PDF, CSV and web-manifest files get their real types.
  - The preview serves the whole site: the project folder for a file in the project, else the nearest folder up
    with an `index.html`. A page in `pages/` loads `../css/site.css` and links back to `../index.html`.
  - Hidden files and folders (`.env`, `.git/`, `.ssh/`, `.npmrc`…) and private keys (`*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_*`) are
    never served to the page's scripts, and a page sitting directly in Downloads, Desktop, Documents or the temp
    folder is refused like one in the home folder.
  - A remote (SFTP) file is never previewed, also from the HTML Preview commands.
  - Editing or saving any file of the site reloads the page, a stylesheet without a reload; closing a file serves
    it from disk again.
  - Previewing a page of another folder no longer breaks the tabs already open; each site has its own address.
  - Open preview tabs no longer tie up the server (a few tabs, or idle connections, stalled page loads), and a page
    whose server has gone backs off and says so instead of polling hundreds of times a second.
  - A Turkish page with many capital İ no longer fails with an error, and the reload script goes before the last
    `</body>`, not into one in a script or comment.
  - Other pages of the site keep their own encoding (Latin-1 no longer turns into �).
  - The preview address changes every time the server starts; only GET and HEAD are answered, with `nosniff`.
  - Status messages tell a server problem from a browser one, say when the chosen browser was missing and the
    default one opened the page, and report a browser that quit at once.
  - More browsers are offered: Chromium (no longer shown as Google Chrome), Brave, Vivaldi, Opera, Firefox
    Developer Edition, Arc, Flatpak and Snap installs, any other Linux browser with a launcher, and per-user
    Windows installs; a browser installed later shows up without reopening the window.
  - Settings → Web names a remembered browser that is no longer installed ("Brave (not found)"), and Doctor's
    Web Browsers row is translated.
  - The open-in-browser button is a real globe, and it appears on an HTML file recognised by its modeline.
- **HTML editing (HTML review: edit).**
  - Templates open as HTML: `.html.erb`, `.erb`, `.ejs`, `.njk`, `.jinja`, `.jinja2`, `.j2`, `.twig`, `.liquid` and
    `.mustache` files are "HTML Template", `.hbs`/`.handlebars` "Handlebars", with the HTML colours, tag auto-close and
    rename, folding, Structure, spell checking, the HTML snippets and `<!-- -->` comments. They are not sent to the
    HTML language server, except Handlebars, which it completes, hovers and formats. A template named after the file
    it renders (`nginx.conf.j2`, `config.yml.erb`) is that file's language.
  - Toggle Comment writes `/* */` in a `<style>` and `//` in a `<script>` instead of `<!-- -->`, and in PHP writes
    `<!-- -->` in the HTML part instead of `//`; a selection that runs from the markup into a script is refused.
  - Enter inside a `<script>` or `<style>` indents after `{`, and a typed `}` steps back to its opener.
  - Folding without the server folds `<DIV>`…`</div>` and a `<script>` holding `a<b`.
  - Spell checking reads `alt`, `title`, `placeholder`, `aria-label` and `aria-description` values, checks the rest of
    a line that holds an inline `<script>`, skips `<code>`, `<kbd>`, `<samp>` and `<var>`, and a `<pre>` mentioned in a
    comment no longer turns checking off for the rest of the file.
  - Structure without the server labels elements as the server does (`header#hero.card`) and lists one-line headings
    and elements with an `id`.
  - Format Document formats HTML without the language server (Editora's own formatter, which keeps `<pre>`,
    `<textarea>`, `<script>` and `<style>` content and your blank lines).
  - Snippets: `!` selects `en`, `doctype` is `<!DOCTYPE html>`, `html5`'s body is indented, `link` is a stylesheet
    link, the obsolete `big`, `command`, `keygen` and `menuitem` are gone; the New File HTML pages agree with them.
- **HTML: install, start-up and status (HTML review, install).** Install for HTML, CSS and JSON now puts
  vscode-langservers-extracted **4.10.0** (pinned, not npm's latest) into Editora's own folder
  (`plugins/lsp/web` under the config folder) instead of `npm install -g`, with the link its HTML server needs to find
  TypeScript's libraries: JavaScript in `<script>` and `on…=""` gets the DOM and standard library again (completion
  after `document.`, parameter help, real hovers), which no npm install of the package had. A blank HTML, CSS or JSON
  command runs that copy first, then PATH. Doctor's HTML row warns when the server in use cannot load those libraries,
  with Update; its version is checked against the pin. Format Document no longer says "Already formatted" when the
  request failed, timed out or was cut off by a restart: it says which. A server whose requests time out twice in a
  row is reported as not responding (with Restart Language Servers), and as responding again once it answers. The
  Node.js chosen in Settings now runs every npm-installed server (HTML, CSS, JSON, YAML, Bash, Pyright…), not only
  TypeScript's, and Doctor's Node.js row counts those servers as needing it. The first HTML or CSS file asks to turn
  on code intelligence, and the install banner says what Install runs and that it needs Node.js (before the click,
  when npm is missing). Doctor's crash tip no longer talks about lemminx outside XML, and a server run by the user's
  own command offers Settings…, not an Install that would change nothing. A `node …/htmlServerNodeMain.js` command is
  shown as vscode-html-language-server, not "node". An extensionless file starting `<!doctype html` or `<html` opens
  as HTML. A loose page of a static site without `package.json` or `.git` is served from the highest folder above it
  holding an `index.html` (below home), so `/css/…` links resolve. HTML files keep their server up to 50,000 lines.
- **XML editing (XML/pom review 3: xmlui).**
  - XML: Generate Grammar…'s two XSD choices work in untrusted folders. lemminx needed the W3C `xml.xsd`, which it
    could not download there; Editora now ships it.
  - Generate Grammar no longer offers "bind with DOCTYPE" on a file that already has a DOCTYPE (an internal subset
    only), which wrote a second one.
  - Bind to Grammar… and Generate Grammar… work on a file whose only `xml-model` is a Schematron rule set.
  - Typing a close tag by hand over the auto-inserted one: Backspace takes back your last character instead of
    deleting (and renaming) the existing tags, `</item >` no longer leaves a stray `>`, HTML tag names match in any
    case, and moving the caret drops the pending join.
  - Go to Definition opens a percent-encoded (`sub%20dir/lib.xsl`) or `file:` include href and an XInclude in the
    default namespace, and says "missing.xsl does not exist" for a target that is not there.
  - The built-in formatter says "Already formatting" to a second Format Document instead of a false "file changed",
    and in large-file mode asks before a format that more than doubles the line count.
  - Settings ▸ LSP ▸ XML: "Keep text as written in" and "XML catalogs" are wider and show their whole value on hover;
    the formatting rows no longer repeat "(XML server only)" under their heading.
- **Shell scripts: setting up the Bash server is one step, and Doctor tells the truth about it** (Bash review,
  install). The first shell script asks once whether to turn code intelligence on. The install banner says what
  Install brings, and Install adds ShellCheck and shfmt with the server; when only those two are missing, the
  script gets an Install banner instead of an echo-line notice the next message overwrote. bash-language-server is
  installed at 5.8.1 (not npm's latest), and the install refuses a Node.js older than 20, which 5.8 needs. Doctor
  shows the version of every npm-installed server, warns with Update below bash-language-server 5.7, warns when a
  server's Node.js is missing or this window gave up on a server after it kept crashing, and offers Restart
  Language Servers on those rows. A crash loop is now an error in the status bar (it raises the unread marker). One
  name, "Bash / Shell", in the banner, status and Doctor; the Settings tool row says ShellCheck; separate Doctor tips
  for ShellCheck (no problems) and shfmt (no formatting).
- **Shell scripts: problems for every open script, and libraries changed on disk are read again** (Bash review,
  sync):
  - Scripts opened while the Bash server starts (a restored session, several files opened at once) all show their
    ShellCheck problems; only the last one did, until it was edited.
  - A Settings ▸ Bash change re-checks every open script, not only the last one touched (bash-language-server 5.6).
  - After Restart Language Servers, background tabs keep their problems instead of waiting to be visited (every
    server).
  - A sourced library changed on disk by git, a terminal or another editor is read again: Go to Definition lands on
    the right line and new functions complete, without a restart.
  - Find References from a call lists that call and leaves out the definition; a function used once no longer jumps
    to its definition.
  - On a line with emoji, ShellCheck squiggles sit under the right characters and "Apply fix" quotes the right word.
- **Language servers hear of file changes in collapsed folders.** Each server's project folder is watched as a whole
  (skipping hidden, dependency and `.gitignore`d folders), not only the folders the Project panel shows expanded, so a
  `git checkout` no longer leaves jdtls, Pyright or lemminx with a stale model.
- **Bash server (Bash review, config):** a project's `bashIde` overrides reach only the servers for that project's
  folders, not scripts opened from another repository, `~/bin` or `/etc`. Container and WSL folders look ShellCheck
  and shfmt up on their own PATH instead of being sent this machine's copies. Scripts outside any repository share
  one Bash server per window (background analysis off) instead of one node process per folder. ShellCheck's SC1071
  ("only supports sh/bash…") is no longer shown on zsh scripts, nor SC2034/SC2154 on a `PKGBUILD`. A file with a
  `# shellcheck shell=…` directive (a sourced `.inc` library) opens as a shell script. ShellCheck arguments are sent
  as a list, so a quoted argument with spaces survives. An explainshell endpoint over plain `http://` to another
  machine is refused (hover sends it the whole command line), and a Bash hover waiting on explainshell gives up
  after 5 seconds with "explainshell did not answer". The Bash card names the rows a project overrides and checks
  the tools the window actually runs; the ShellCheck-arguments and `.editorconfig` texts say what the server really
  does (it already follows sourced files; any shfmt key in `.editorconfig` replaces all the shfmt options).
- **Shell scripts with the Bash language server (Bash review: editing UI).**
  - Rename on a command (`echo`, `cd`) is refused: "echo is a command, not a function or variable defined in your
    scripts". It used to rewrite every call in the file with no preview. A new name must be a shell name (a function
    may also have `-`, `.` and `:`).
  - Format Document on a script shfmt cannot parse says why, with the line ("Could not format: line 5: `for`
    statement must end with `done`"), and points at the shebang or the shfmt dialect for a `#!/bin/sh` script with
    bashisms. It used to say "Already formatted". A format that changes nothing says "Already formatted" for every
    server and leaves the file clean; a selection on a server without range formatting says the whole file was
    formatted.
  - The problem counter counts notes (information and hints, muted) as a third number, so ShellCheck's quoting
    advice no longer shows a green check; the check means no problems at all, and the counter's arrows go through
    every problem. A zsh script shows "Not checked: ShellCheck has no zsh mode". Applies to every language server.
  - ShellCheck quick fixes say what they do ("Fix SC2006: Use $(...) notation instead of legacy backticks"), with
    the column when two would read alike. Suppressions are tagged **Suppress** and listed after the fixes, and with
    bash-language-server 5.6 (which offers none) "Disable SC2086 for this command" inserts the directive above the
    line.
  - Completion ranks keywords and snippets first, then the script's functions and variables, builtins, and PATH
    commands last, with a detail saying which; after `$` it offers only variables. Editora's own shell snippets
    (`case`, `function`, `while`, `echo`) stay in the list beside the server's word of the same name. Without the
    server, the script's own function and variable names are offered after the snippets.
  - Block Tab / Indent Lines no longer indents the shebang, a here-doc's text or its delimiter (a `<<-` here-doc
    moves by tabs only), or the inside of a multi-line string.
  - A hover pages with Page Down / Page Up (and Emacs's C-v / M-v), and a man page gets its 80 columns.
  - Next Problem onto a ShellCheck error no longer leaves the red unread-error badge.
  - The completion documentation panel loses the Markdown preview's margins and language tag; a two-line snippet
    description shows its first line in the row.
  - "1 symbols" in Go to Symbol in Workspace; the rename preview's Select all / Select none are no longer cut.
  - Keymaps: CUA gets F2 (Rename), F12 / Shift+F12 (Go to Definition / Find References), Ctrl+. (Code Actions)
    and Shift+Alt+F (Format Document); Sublime gets Ctrl+Shift+R (Go to Symbol) and Shift+Alt+F; Emacs gets
    `M-g s` (Go to Symbol in Workspace).
- **Narrowing and widening are finished in the frame they happen in.** The Structure window's Narrow to Fold
  Region toggle (and C-x n n / n f / n w) swapped the text in unstyled: the code showed plain until the next
  highlight pass, the fold gutter kept the old lines, and on widening the outline showed raw fold blocks for a
  moment, about a quarter second after narrowing a 1,600-line file and over half a second after widening it (three
  quarters on a 10,000-line one). The swap now keeps the colours, folds and outline symbols, and widening keeps the
  region's lines where they were on screen instead of scrolling from the top of the file to put the caret at the
  bottom edge.
- **Format Document follows the file's save rules.** Format Document and Format Selection now send the file's
  EditorConfig `trim_trailing_whitespace` and `insert_final_newline` (or the project's) to the language server, so a
  formatted file already looks the way saving writes it. lemminx adds the final newline only when asked. Tab re-indent
  and on-type formatting leave them out.
- **One malformed pom no longer stops Maven dependency completion.** lemminx-maven kept a malformed pom in its
  workspace with no project, and every groupId/artifactId/version completion after the first threw on it, leaving
  only `<!--` and `<![CDATA[`. Editora now takes each pom that is malformed on disk out of the server's workspace,
  asks again, and names the file in the status bar ("Left out broken/pom.xml …"). It looks where lemminx-maven
  looks (`pom*.xml`, `*pom.xml` and `*.pom`, ten folders deep, `node_modules` and `build` included), and acts only
  when the server really failed, so an honest empty answer changes nothing. When the pom is well-formed again
  (saved here, or fixed by a checkout), or the server still holds a pom fixed after it broke, only that project's
  Maven server restarts, and its open poms move to the new one at once.
- **XML and pom.xml trust (review 3).** Where the native XML server cannot run, the Java one Editora falls back to
  no longer loads the Maven extension, so a pom in an untrusted folder is no longer resolved and its plugins no longer
  run; an XML command that would load lemminx-maven is not started, and the status bar says why. Trusting or revoking
  a folder moves every open pom.xml at once, background tabs included, and a revoked pom keeps its diagnostics. Trust
  This Folder on a file outside the project no longer trusts the project. A pom in an untrusted folder without the
  Maven server gets one offer to install it, saying it runs only in trusted folders. The blocked-schema status names
  only what would help. Doctor's lemminx-maven store row follows a `<localRepository>` set in settings.xml. A pre-pin
  lemminx path with arguments keeps them, and Settings shows a pre-pin copy as an amber warning.
- **Language servers get the whole file when it opens.** Python, Java and XML files reached their server empty and
  were then filled in, so an XML file flashed a false "Premature end of file" error, the file was analysed twice,
  and quick fixes and generated schemas used a four-space indent in a two-space file. The indent a server is told
  now also follows the file as you edit it.
- **XML: code lenses refresh after a settings change**, and lemminx's refresh request no longer logs an internal
  error.
- **XML: a relative schema association no longer applies to files outside the project**, where it failed with an
  error naming an internal Editora folder.
- **XML is no longer guessed from `.mod`, `.sch`, `.props`, `.targets` and `.fo` alone**: such a file is XML only
  when its text starts with `<`, so a Modula-2 module or a KiCad schematic opens as plain text.
- **The status bar and Problems say XML, JSON, YAML, HTML, CSS, SQL, TOML, C++, C#** (and other acronyms) instead
  of "Xml" or "Cpp", and plain text reads "Plain Text".
- **XML formatting (XML/pom review 2: format).**
  - Format Document and Tab use lemminx again. Editora's XML settings left out `format.enabled`, so lemminx never
    offered formatting: every Format Document fell back to the built-in formatter, Tab never got the server's
    indent, and the four XML formatting settings did nothing.
  - lemminx now gets vscode-xml's whole set of format defaults, so it keeps up to two blank lines, keeps a
    multi-line start tag such as a pom's `<project …>` header on its lines, and leaves comment and CDATA lines alone.
  - New **Keep text as written in** (Settings ▸ LSP ▸ XML, `xmlFormatPreserveSpace`, vscode-xml's list): elements
    whose text the XML server leaves exactly as written. Settings schema 150 → 151 (additive).
  - Tab on a line that opens an element (`<d>` with its `</d>` below) re-indents it instead of typing spaces into
    the tag.
  - The built-in formatter (no XML server) keeps blank lines, at most two in a row, and keeps a trailing comment on
    the line it follows. It formats off the UI thread, puts the caret back on the character it was on, and its
    no-undo notice for a large file says "Format Document".
  - The XML settings card has Validation, Formatting (XML server) and Structure headings; the formatting rows say
    they need the XML server, and "Wrap long text: off" no longer claims text is left as it is. The Structure
    element limit applies without the server too.
- **XML and HTML: typing a close tag by hand no longer renames another tag.** Typing `</b>` before an outer `</p>`
  gave `<bp>…</b>p>`, and a typo in a closing name (`</itme>`) renamed the open tag. Only the closer of the innermost
  open element is joined, and a name that turns out different becomes a tag of its own.
- **XML: Bind to Grammar… on a file that is already bound** says what it is bound to instead of writing a second,
  duplicate binding; a file with a DOCTYPE binds a DTD by `xml-model`.
- **XML: Go to Definition on an `xsl:include` or `xsl:import` href** opens the stylesheet, as documented.
- **A DTD no longer offers an XML tree preview** that called the file not well-formed.
- **Banner buttons no longer shrink to "…".** Install and Not now on the XML install banner (and every other
  banner) keep their labels; the message wraps instead, and the XML banner is shorter.
- **pom.xml and the Maven server (XML/pom review 2).** A pom.xml served by the plain XML server now offers the
  Maven server (what it adds, about 16 MB), or Settings… when your own command for it is missing; a pom in a folder
  you have not trusted is left to the trust offer. "Reset to default" on the Maven server command keeps Editora's
  installed copy instead of asking for a second download. A Maven project beside the open one gets one server, not
  one per module, and an SSH/WSL/container host is never sent this machine's classpath (its plain XML server serves
  the pom unless the host has an `lsp.maven-pom` tool). The Structure window names dependencies and plugins by
  `groupId:artifactId` with the Maven server on; a plugin's "managed in" hover link opens, and hover links go to
  the line they name (`#L28,22`). "Extract as new property in parent" works while the parent is open (unsaved
  parent: refused with a reason). When one malformed pom stops dependency completion, the status bar names it.
  XML: Revalidate File and lemminx's client commands work on a pom; a model diagnostic no longer shows the pom's
  path as its source.
- **XML and pom.xml: folder trust.** A pom.xml in a folder you have not trusted no longer reaches the Maven pom
  server (lemminx-maven), which fetched the parents, plugins and extensions it named — from repositories the pom
  itself named — and could run their code. It is edited with the plain XML server until you trust the folder; its
  tab says "Maven-aware editing is off until you trust this folder" with **Trust Folder**, which moves it to the
  Maven server. Revoking trust stops that server on the folder. A pom outside every trusted folder stays on the XML
  server.
  - **Workspace: Trust This Folder** (palette) trusts the active file's folder, and an XML file whose schema was not
    downloaded because its folder is not trusted offers Trust Folder on the file: an XML-only folder had no way to
    be trusted. Downloads turn on without a restart.
  - The Maven POM schemas (4.0.0 and 4.1.0) are bundled: a pom validates and completes with schema downloads off,
    without the two errors on line 2.
  - "Use the Maven Central index" is now **Search Maven Central when completing pom.xml coordinates**, and says that
    what you type is sent to search.maven.org (there is no index download).
  - Doctor: a crashing or failing server's row has the Install… its tip names; the XML schema cache sits under its
    server and is shown when only the pom server is on; lemminx-maven's artifact store (`~/.m2/.lemminx-maven`) has
    its own row with Clear and Reveal, and the pom server keeps it under Editora's home.
  - The status bar says "files outside the project" rather than Editora's internal `loose-files` folder.
  - Settings says when Editora's own server copy predates version records, as Doctor does; a stored path to an
    old per-platform lemminx copy is cleared (Settings schema 150 → 151), since a blank command runs that copy.
  - After the XML install falls back to the Java lemminx, the native copy that cannot run is removed and a blank
    XML command keeps the Java one.
- **Terminal: a selection keeps its text when the terminal is resized.** JediTerm moves a selection itself when a
  shorter window pushes rows into history, and the terminal moved it again: after a splitter drag the highlight sat
  rows above the selected text, and Copy copied those rows. A block selection is dropped on a resize, whose reflow
  moves its columns.
- **Terminal (from Termina):** closing a terminal no longer holds the window for up to half a second each; the
  cursor no longer vanishes at the end of a line typed to its full width; Nerd Font icons (eza, lsd, powerline) are
  drawn in an installed Nerd Font rather than the first fallback face that maps them, which put a stray `¯` beside
  some names; rows are tall enough for the font, so descenders are not clipped; a block cursor redraws its
  character in the cell's own font and colour; a binary file's flood of bells is one flash; entering or leaving a
  full-screen program drops a selection made on the other screen; `file://` links naming this machine open as
  local files; the keypad's arrow keys work; box drawing and other one-cell text is drawn in one call per run.
- **Java: Go to Super Method answers where the caret is.** On an anonymous class method's name, modifiers or
  `@Override` line in an initializer or a library class, it opened `Object.java` or the enclosing method's super
  method; on a class whose line ends in a `// comment`, its first method's. A caret just before a lambda's `(`,
  inside its `->`, or on `String[]::new`'s type or `Collections::<String>emptyList`'s name goes to the functional
  method.
- **Java: Go to Super Method reads more generics right.** `new java.util.Comparator<>()` after another anonymous
  class, or `new Holder.Pair<>()`, said "No super method found", as did a `<>` assigned to a wildcard type
  (`Comparator<? super String>`) and a supertype named twice (`List<List<Double>>`). A method's own type parameter of
  any name (`<Out>`) pairs with the override's, a raw supertype's (`extends Store`) stands for its erasure, type
  arguments carry through a library interface (`Names extends List<String>`: `add(Integer)` overrides nothing), and
  an open supertype file is read with its unsaved edits.
- **Java: Go to Super Method checks the type an anonymous class instantiates.** A `<>` anonymous class of a nested
  type (`new Outer.Mid.Sink<>() {…}`) opened an unrelated JDK type or method (`java.util.stream.Sink`,
  `Consumer.accept`) or the outer class, from its methods and from its own header, brace or fields. What jdtls answers
  there is now checked against the name as written, and the type is found through the file's import, the variable's
  declared type, its outer type's outline (also a jar class's without sources) or a supertype's (an inherited member
  type); when nothing checks out, it says so. Go to Definition on such a type name opens the checked type too. In an
  initializer's or a library class's anonymous method, the caret in the parameter list (an annotated or a wrapped
  one), the Javadoc or a `//` comment right above opened `Object.java`; it is that method's now. The anonymous class's
  header, from its type's name to its `{`, or a field in it goes to the type it instantiates (not that type's
  constructor, and not `Object`'s), and an interface's anonymous `hashCode()` to `Object.hashCode`. A paste into a
  text block escapes its backslashes, and into a char literal its backslash and quote. On a one-line class a later method is
  itself, a wrapped class header with a trailing comment is the class's, and `Collections::<List<String>>emptyList`
  goes to `Supplier.get`. A class's supertypes leave out `java.lang.Object`, as in IntelliJ: `class X implements
  Runnable` opens `Runnable.java`, and a plain class says "No supertype found".
- **Java: Go to Super Method's generics at the edges.** A jar interface without sources whose type variable has a
  longer name (`LKeyed<Key>`) is read from its decompiled header, so its override is found and an overload with another
  type is not; a raw `new Store() {…}` assigned to a `Store<String>` is raw; a supertype open in another window is read
  with its unsaved edits.
- **Java: the import verdict.** A pom broken after a compile error had been built read as "the project did not
  import", every file "Not checked"; a Gradle build that failed beside a Maven one in one folder marked both. A
  reactor module whose pom.xml does not parse, and a broken pom with a loose file opened first, now say the project
  did not import; a pom that does not parse is named with its line and column, and a Gradle script that does not
  compile with its error, not "1 error".
- **Paste with imports asks again when jdtls answers before it has the paste**, and sends the file the text was
  copied from, so its imports decide ambiguous names (`Duration`).
- **Closing a focused Doctor, Welcome or viewer tab from the keyboard leaves the keyboard in the tab shown**, not on
  the toolbar's New button; the Welcome page takes the focus itself, with its recent list current, not its first
  entry.
- **Doctor's missing-sources hint reads more build layouts**: a module inheriting its parent's release or managed
  compiler plugin, a Spring Boot parent with its version first, an MR-jar's per-execution release, every included
  Gradle project, a version catalog, a `buildSrc` convention plugin; a Gradle toolchain wins over a variable named
  `release`.
- **XML: the lemminx install is pinned and checked.** Install… downloads vscode-xml 0.29.3's lemminx (0.31.2) instead
  of whatever `releases/latest` was, refuses a zip or a program whose SHA-256 is not the release's, takes exactly
  the program (not any file whose name starts with "lemminx"), and no longer asks for `tar` (every asset is a zip).
  It writes an install receipt, so Settings and Doctor show the version and Doctor offers Update when a later Editora
  moves the pin; a copy installed before receipts is offered Update once.
- **XML: Reset no longer disconnects Editora's lemminx.** The install leaves the XML command blank, and a blank
  command (or a stale path into Editora's own XML folder) runs Editora's copy before anything on PATH.
- **XML: a lemminx that cannot run here says why.** Install asks the new server to answer a request first; on a
  system whose C library is too old (lemminx needs glibc 2.34) it installs nothing and says so — or, when the pom.xml
  server is installed, XML runs its Java lemminx instead. A server that exits as soon as it starts now gives its own
  first words in the crash notice, Settings and Doctor, instead of "found" and "OK", and Install treats it as missing.
- **XML install banner.** Not offered while the XML server is switched off; a configured XML command that is
  missing leads to Settings instead of an Install that would overwrite it; it says what the server adds and what
  Install downloads (about 17 MB, from Red Hat's vscode-xml release on GitHub); and "Not now" holds for every XML
  file of the window, not one tab. With language servers off, the first XML file asks once whether to turn them on.
- **XML: DTDs, RELAX NG schemas and other XML dialects are XML.** `.dtd .ent .mod .rng .fo .xspec .sch .csproj
  .vbproj .fsproj .props .targets .nuspec .resx .xaml .xlf .xliff .plist .xul .kml .gpx .tld .jnlp .xmi .ditamap
  .dita` open with XML highlighting, folding, comments and the XML language server instead of as spell-checked
  plain text, and a file with no telling extension that starts with `<?xml` (an `AndroidManifest`) is XML too.
  `go.mod` stays plain text; `.xhtml` stays HTML.
- **XML: Go to Definition opens the schema.** On a `schemaLocation`, a DOCTYPE's DTD, an `xml-model` href or an
  `xsl:include`, Go to Definition and Ctrl/Cmd-click open the referenced file; on an element or attribute name they
  go to its XSD declaration instead of the element's own end tag.
- **XML: one language server per window.** XML files outside the project, in any number of folders or Maven
  modules, share one lemminx instead of starting one each.
- **XML: files up to 100,000 lines and 5 MB keep the language server** (it stopped at 10,000), and the large-file
  notice now says that folding, Structure, spell check and the language server are off too; Structure says why it is
  empty.
- **XML: lemminx's commands and quick fixes work.** New palette commands XML: Revalidate File, XML: Revalidate
  All Open Files and XML: Bind to Grammar…; the "Bind to existing grammar/schema" quick fix picks an XSD, DTD or
  RELAX NG file and binds it with `xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation`, a DOCTYPE or `xml-model`; lemminx's buttons on
  its notifications and its client commands are carried out.
- **XML: "Generate … and bind" quick fixes work.** Each of lemminx's fixes that writes an XSD, DTD or RelaxNG
  grammar for a file without one failed with "Could not apply" and left an empty tab for the grammar file; the
  grammar is now written and bound. Any refused edit closes the tabs it opened, and one that names a path Editora
  cannot place says which.
- **XML completion lists the schema's elements and values first.** "Insert Comment" and "Insert CDATA" were
  preselected after `<`, so Enter inserted a comment; completion now orders the server's sort keys ignoring case,
  as VS Code does.
- **XML: Tab re-indents a line while the XML server runs**, and falls back to the usual smart Tab when the server
  gives no indent; it did nothing on a non-blank line.
- **XML: a close tag typed by hand joins the one tag auto-close inserted** instead of leaving `<from>x</</from>`.
- **Show Documentation and Show Problem at Caret show the whole problem at the caret**, above any documentation:
  lemminx's list of the allowed elements or values was cut off in the status line, and hover said there was
  nothing.
- **XML: no dangling "Code:" at the end of problem messages**, and Rename says it cannot rename where the server
  declines instead of opening a dialog that does nothing.
- **XML: "Minify XML" is no longer offered as the fix for a problem**; it stays under Generate, and in Code Actions
  on a line without one.
- **XML: a schema changed outside Editora revalidates the XML files that use it**, also in a collapsed Project
  folder; the errors stayed until the next keystroke.
- **XML server settings** (Settings ▸ LSP, the XML card): Editora now sends lemminx its settings at start, pushes a
  change to the running server and answers its configuration questions, where before it sent nothing at all.
  **Download schemas** (`xmlSchemaDownloads`: never / only in trusted folders, the default / always), **Files without
  a grammar** (`xmlNoGrammar`: nothing, the default / hint / warning), **XML catalogs** (`xmlCatalogs`; a relative
  path is looked for in each project's root), **Schema associations** (`xmlFileAssociations`,
  `*.myconf.xml=schemas/myconf.xsd`), formatting (**Wrap long text**, off by default, wraps at the fill column;
  **Attributes**; **Empty elements**; **Space before />**) and the **Structure element limit** (`xmlSymbolLimit`,
  5,000). Settings schema 148 → 149 (additive).
- **Doctor ▸ XML schema cache**: the size and folder of the schemas the XML server downloaded, with **Clear**.
- **XML: opening a file no longer downloads every schema it names from any host.** lemminx fetched each
  `xsi:schemaLocation`, DOCTYPE and `xml-model` grammar over http or https as soon as a file opened, in any folder.
  Downloads now happen only in trusted folders by default; elsewhere the file says the download is off and the status
  line says where to change it. External entities are never resolved.
- **XML: downloaded schemas are kept under Editora's config folder** (`cache/lemminx`), not in `~/.lemminx`, so a
  portable or test configuration no longer shares the user's cache, and settings export leaves it out.
- **XML: a file without a schema or DTD no longer adds "No grammar constraints" to Problems** (SVG, XSLT, FXML, plain
  config files); Settings can bring the hint back.
- **XML: quick fixes and generated grammars are indented like the file**: lemminx's tab-size and spaces questions were
  answered with nothing.
- **XML: the "document symbols have been limited to 5000 items" notice names the setting that raises the limit.**
- **XML: Format Document no longer wraps text at a fixed 100 columns.** Text is left on its lines unless Wrap long
  text is on, which wraps at the editor's fill column; XSD and DTD files get lemminx's reference code lenses when
  Code Lens is on.
- **Java: Go to Super Method reads type arguments.** In `interface StrStore extends Store<String>`, `save(Integer)`
  opened `Store.save(T)`, and `Multi.accept(Integer)` offered a second, wrong branch; `T` now stands for `String`
  there, so neither does, and `take(T[])` takes only a `String[]`. It also works on a method reference
  (`String::length`) and in a lambda's parameters, both the functional interface's method; in an initializer's or a
  library field's anonymous class written with `<>`; in a one-line nested class or field initializer, whose
  `static` or `private` was read as the method's; and it never lands on the method itself
  (`new java.util.Comparator<>() {…}`). "Looking for super methods…" no longer stays under the picker, and a
  dependency's class rebuilt in place is read again.
- **Java: a pom.xml that does not parse when the project is first opened is a failed import.** jdtls reported the
  project as imported and checked every Java file for syntax only, under "Loaded and ready"; it now says the project
  did not import, why, and each file's counter says it is not checked. A file outside the source folders is not
  counted.
- **Java: a window that joins after a failed import counts it as one error**, as the first window does, not two.
- **Doctor's missing-sources hint names the JDK Maven compiles with**: the compiler plugin's `<release>` over a
  property, no profile's properties, a property from the parent pom, Spring Boot's default; in Gradle, a release in
  an included project's build, and `prerelease` is no release.
- **View: Focus Next Editor Group puts the keyboard in that group's editor.** It focused the tab's container, so
  typed keys went nowhere and the arrows switched tabs.
- **Closing the last file tab beside the Welcome tab leaves the keyboard on the Welcome page**, not on the toolbar's
  New button, where a Space opened a new buffer.
- **XML: Structure outlines every element, named by its attribute.** Without the XML server an XSD or XSLT outline
  listed only the namespace prefix (`xs line 2`, `xs line 3`) and no one-line elements; every element is now listed
  as `xs:element name="note"` or `xsl:template match="/"`. With the server, the outline loses lemminx's "Grammars",
  "Cache: false" and "Binding: …" rows and schema rows carry their `name`.
- **XML: Format Document works without the XML server**: a built-in formatter puts one element per line in the
  file's own indentation and leaves text, CDATA and `xml:space="preserve"` content exactly as written.
- **XML and SVG previews say where they fail**: the parser's message with a "Line 2, column 5" link that jumps there,
  instead of "Could not render this SVG".
- **New File ▸ XML and SVG start with a skeleton, and XML Schema and XSLT are new entries**; New From Template adds
  "XML Schema (XSD)", "XSLT Stylesheet" and "XML Bound to a Schema". XML has 25 snippets (was 6), and element,
  comment, CDATA and the XSLT/XSD containers wrap the selection, so Surround With works in XML.
- **XML: `<!ELEMENT>`, `<!ATTLIST>` and `<!NOTATION>` declarations are highlighted**, like `<!ENTITY>`, in a
  DOCTYPE's internal subset and in a bare DTD.
- **VS Code keymap: Shift+Alt+F (Shift+Option+F on macOS) formats the document**, as in VS Code.
- **A jump shows its own column**: Go to Definition, Structure clicks and search hits kept the old horizontal
  scroll, so after the end of a long line a jump near a line start landed with the first characters cut off, and a
  jump far along a long line left the caret off screen.
- **Java: more of the import verdict.** jdtls's "… does not exist" errors for a file outside the source folders no
  longer turn a later pom break into "the project did not import"; a Gradle build that fails in `tools/` of a Maven
  project is that folder's, the rest stays checked; a pom.xml that does not parse beside another build is said, and
  its files are "Not checked" rather than "Loaded and ready". A module's pom.xml saved or changed (a `git pull`) in a
  collapsed folder now reaches jdtls, so its classpath updates without Reload Project Configuration. A broken Gradle
  settings file names its cause, two Kotlin script errors name the first, a script is named by its file name, and a
  pom's line and column read in the interface's language. A settings file that `include`s a folder that does not
  exist, or `includeBuild`s one, is a failed import again; a pom with a dependency missing its `<version>` or
  `<artifactId>`, a parent Maven cannot resolve, or `<packaging>pom</packaging>` over Java sources says the project
  (or that module) did not import, naming the cause, rather than "Loaded and ready" over files that were never
  checked; once such a pom is fixed, saved here or changed by a git pull, the project's workspace is cleaned so it
  imports again (a restart reused the broken project, and a pull left false errors under "Loaded and ready"); a build that failed in one folder of a project is named with that folder; and a Gradle
  dependency that cannot be fetched is a build with problems, not a failed import. In a tree of
  more than 2,000 folders, a module's pom.xml past the watched ones still reaches jdtls when saved or seen in the
  Project panel, and build output folders (`target`, `build`) no longer use up the build-file watcher's share.
- **Focus and paste.** Window ▸ Buffer: Next and the Switcher onto the Welcome, Doctor or an image tab focus that page;
  the toolbar's New button had the focus, and Space opened a buffer. A paste's imports no longer depend on a pause
  after it: typing right after the pasted text keeps them. Code copied from a file that was deleted or moved since
  still imports what the text alone needs. In the Emacs keymap, a kill (C-k, M-d, zap) records its file as a cut does,
  and M-y adds the imports the swapped-in text needs, with an older ring entry's own file; once those imports land,
  M-y still works. View ▸ Doctor or Welcome on a tab already open, and an image or PDF opened again, focus that tab.
  Buffer: Next goes round the split group it is in. A paste into a Java string literal is escaped, as in IntelliJ: a
  pasted `C:\temp "x"` becomes `C:\\temp \"x\"`, and pasted lines are joined with `+`; text copied from inside a
  string literal pastes as it is.
- **Small fixes.** Doctor's JDK reading follows a multi-line Gradle `include(…)` or Groovy `include 'a',` list, a
  convention plugin rather than buildSrc's own toolchain, `providers.gradleProperty("javaVersion")` and a bare
  `JavaLanguageVersion.of(javaVersion)`, and no longer takes an aggregator above a
  Spring Boot module for its parent. A drag-move right after opening a file the move edits is asked of jdtls once more
  instead of failing with "the file changed". The bundled grammars' "character class has ']' without escape" warnings
  no longer reach the Debug Log, and a Gradle build file no longer logs two missing-grammar warnings: its Javadoc
  comments are highlighted. Go to Super Method into a file open only in another window, with unsaved edits, lands on
  the method's line in the copy it opens, and it no longer re-reads a JDK class's source for every supertype.
- **Structure narrowing and jumps.** With Narrow to fold region on, clicking another symbol in the Structure window
  keeps that row selected instead of flickering back to the first row. Jumps (Structure, Go to Line, definitions,
  search hits and the scrollbar stripe marks) leave two lines of context below the sticky-scroll rows, so the
  target line is no longer half hidden under them, and each sticky row is now exactly one code line tall.
- **Snippet pickers no longer flicker.** Surround With and Insert Snippet stopped toggling a horizontal scroll bar
  while the selection moved over a snippet with a long description.
